name: Garage door repair & installation — independent, NW Cook / DuPage (residential + HOA/light-commercial B2B)
summary: Job-based home service (Stage E refresh 2026-11-28). Each 'customer' is one paid job (monthly churn = 100%, so active customers = jobs in the month; no recurring ARPC). Demand = company inbound leads (Google LSA/search, GBP, referrals, HOA/CAM, inspector and realtor requests) ramping over 30 months to a single-territory plateau calibrated to franchise unit revenues (Access, ProLift, Precision FDDs). The founder (not yet a technician) trains in months 1-2 and then works the first van; technicians are hired by capacity once jobs exceed ~60/month. Parts/doors are COGS; technician + van running cost is staff cost. Operating profit is before owner compensation and INCLUDES the founder's unpaid field labour (SDE basis).
evidence_notes: Revenue density: Access Garage Doors 2025 FDD — franchised units average $226k (yr1), $731k (yr2), $1.02M (yr3); COGS 46-47% of sales [B, DF-S001]. ProLift 2025 FDD — 40 franchised units avg $511k, middle-50% avg $424k, bottom quartile $162k [B, DF-S002]. Precision 2026 FDD smallest territory band (91k-230k single-family homes) median $858k; avg ticket $1,213 (2024: $706) [B, C8-S019/C8-S020].

Territory size: the 8 launch suburbs (Arlington Heights, Palatine, Schaumburg, Elk Grove Village, Hoffman Estates, Mount Prospect, Rolling Meadows, Lombard) hold ~109k one-unit homes; an 18-suburb NW Cook/central DuPage cluster ~220k [C, E-WS18035-S014] — i.e., inside Precision's smallest band.
Owner economics (seller-claimed, D): NW Chicago suburbs garage door firm, 1 employee, revenue $472k, SDE $171k [DF-S004]; St. Louis firm, 7 employees, revenue $2.27M, cash flow $317k (14%) [DF-S005].

Technician pay: BLS/O*NET 2025 Mechanical Door Repairers, Chicago MSA median $65,090; 25th pct $51,300 [C, DF-S006]; PayScale Chicago garage-door technician avg base ~$49.6k [D, E-WS18035-S013]. Loaded +25% = E.

Lead cost (Stage E re-fetch of DF-S008, Aug 2026): Searchlight LSA average $49/lead entering 2026, Q1 2026 $45, April $59; non-branded search $173/lead; branded $66; blended $145 (11 contractors, Jan-Apr 2026); commercial overhead-door search CPL $300-600 [D, E-WS18035-S006]. CORRECTION: the '38% LSA book rate / $198 per paying customer' figure Stage D attributed to this source is not on the page.

Channel access: garage-door LSA advertisers in the US must pass Google Advanced Verification (video call; typically 6-8 weeks) plus service-professional background checks [B, E-WS18035-S001/S002] — first LSA lead realistically month 3.

Gross margin CORRECTION: Stage D's 65% base margin is inconsistent with its own $575 ticket (70/15/15 repair/opener/door mix). Re-derived: repairs ~28-33% parts (DDM public springs median $52 [B, DF-S012]), openers ~55-75% (DDM public $456-880 [B]), doors ~50% (Access COGS 46-47% [B, DF-S001]) => blended parts cost ~42% at $575 (GM 58%); 48% at $450 with public-price parts (GM 52%); ~38% at $700 with dealer pricing (GM 62%).

Chicago price band: Raynor Door Co. (Northfield) June 2026 guide — torsion pair $250-400, single $200-300, extension pair $150-300 [D, E-WS18035-S009, directly fetched; Stage D had only a search summary].

Not modelled: light-commercial / HOA preventive-maintenance contracts and NFPA 80 fire-door drop tests (recurring; see playbook side calculation, E), seasonality (installs slower Jan-Feb; spring failures peak in cold snaps, E).
Churn-based stress tests and the churn tornado bar are not meaningful here (churn is structurally 100% in a job-based model); read CAC, ticket, margin, labour, hiring-threshold and demand tests.

drivers.sales_start_delay_months__source: Founder must train before selling (C.H.I. 4-day residential course $550 [B, E-WS18035-S010]; DDM in-person training discontinued [B, E-WS18035-S011]) and LSA Advanced Verification typically takes 6-8 weeks [B, E-WS18035-S002]; entity, Home Repair Act insurance, SSC account (5-7 business days [B, E-WS18035-S008]). Stage D used 1 month (Correction).
drivers.sales_cycle_months__source: Emergency repair calls convert same day (Stage C memo; homeowner urgency).
drivers.founder_ramp_months__source: Months for inbound lead flow to reach plateau (reviews, LSA ranking, B2B accounts). Access Garage Doors franchised units: yr1 avg $226k, yr2 $731k, yr3 $1.02M, yr4 $1.20M [B, DF-S001] — an independent without brand/call centre ramps no faster (E).
drivers.founder_leads_per_month__source: Company inbound leads/month at plateau, back-solved from single-territory franchise revenues [B, DF-S001, DF-S002, C8-S019]: cons ~58 jobs x $450 = ~$0.31M/yr (ProLift middle-50% avg $424k); base ~133 x $575 = ~$0.92M (Access yr-3 avg $1.02M; Precision smallest-band median $858k); opt ~181 x $700 = ~$1.52M (Precision smallest-band avg $1.38M). CORRECTION: Stage D optimistic 330 leads (~$1.8M/yr, 31% y3 margin) exceeded every comparable; trimmed to 280. Independent without brand/call centre reaches franchise-median, not average, volume in base (E).
drivers.lead_to_proposal_pct__source: Lead -> booked visit. Emergency garage-door calls book at high rates (E). CORRECTION: Stage D cited a 'Searchlight LSA book rate 38%' [DF-S008] that is not on the source page when re-fetched (E-WS18035-S006); evidence downgraded D->E. LSA leads include spam/wrong-service calls (disputable).
drivers.proposal_to_win_pct__source: Booked visit -> paid job (diagnosis on site; most repairs sold on the spot).
drivers.rep_new_customers_per_month__source: No sales reps: demand is inbound; technicians are capacity-triggered staff.
drivers.referral_new_per_100_active__source: Repeat/referral jobs per 100 jobs in prior month on top of inbound leads (E); HOA boards and inspectors re-refer.
drivers.monthly_churn_pct__source: Structural: each customer = one job (job-based model).
drivers.onetime_revenue_per_new_customer__source: Average ticket. Precision system avg $706 (CY2024) and $1,213 (CY2025) incl. upsell-heavy premium brand [B, C8-S019/S020]; Raynor Door (Northfield) June 2026 Chicago guide: torsion pair $250-400 [D, E-WS18035-S009]; A1 quotes $350-750 single spring [D, DF-S037]; mix assumed 70% repairs / 15% openers / 15% doors by count (E).
drivers.gross_margin_pct__source: Unused (no recurring revenue); set equal to one-time margin.
drivers.onetime_gross_margin_pct__source: Gross margin after parts/doors only (labour is staff). CORRECTION from Stage D (0.55/0.65/0.70): re-derived from the ticket mix — repairs 28-33% parts at DDM public prices [B, DF-S012], openers 55-75% [B, DF-S012], doors ~50% (Access COGS 46-47% [B, DF-S001]); cons assumes public-price parts (no dealer account), opt assumes SSC/Clopay dealer pricing (MISSING). Component prices B; mix E => C overall.
drivers.variable_opex_pct_revenue__source: Card processing ~3% + fuel ~3% of revenue (Junk King fuel 3.3% of sales as truck-trade analogue [B, WS18-S001]).
drivers.cac_per_new_customer__source: Per paid job (applied to all jobs incl. referrals). Re-derived with 2026 data [D, E-WS18035-S006]: ~60% LSA at $45-59/lead, ~20% non-branded search at $173/lead, ~20% referral/B2B/GBP organic at $0 => ~$64/lead; at ~55% lead-to-paid-job => ~$115/job (~20% of ticket). Stage D base $100 (Correction: LSA CPL now $45-59, not $15-49). Angi shared leads are worse (vendor says each lead is resold to 3-5 pros [D, E-WS18035-S007]; FTC 2023 order on HomeAdvisor lead-quality claims [A, E-WS18035-S003]) and are not in the base mix.
drivers.fixed_marketing_per_month__source: Website, Google Business Profile tools, review software, van wrap amortisation, BNI/association dues.
drivers.dso_days__source: Homeowners pay at completion; HOA/CAM invoices net-30 (~15% of revenue).
drivers.inventory_days_cogs__source: Springs, cables, rollers, openers carried on vans/shelf; doors ordered per job with deposit.
drivers.dpo_days__source: New accounts start COD/card; SSC dealer accounts by application [B, DF-S011]; Raynor requires approved credit terms [B, DF-S009].
drivers.start_capital_injection__source: Set to the base-case peak funding need (smallest injection keeping base-case cash >= 0) per Stage E standardization.
drivers.ev_multiple__source: Operating profit here is SDE-like (before owner comp). Asking prices: $550k on $171k SDE = 3.2x [D, DF-S004]; $1.395M on $317k cash flow = 4.4x [D, DF-S005]. Asking > sold and both are mature firms; new-entrant multiple haircut to 2.5x base (E).
drivers.lt_growth_y6_pct__source: Single territory is at plateau by year 3 (Access yr3->yr4 +18% then flattening [B, DF-S001]); years 6+ growth = price (~3%) plus a light-commercial/PM line or adjacent suburbs. Conservative = inflation-only; optimistic = second territory.
drivers.lt_growth_decay__source: Standard Atlas decay; growth fades as the territory saturates.
drivers.incremental_roic_pct__source: Growth capital = vans ($30k/tech, E), working capital (~2-week cycle) and the ramp losses of a new territory/line. Base y3 op / peak funding in this model ~1.0x for a whole new territory incl. founder labour; a second territory needs a paid manager, so 0.5 base, 0.3 cons, 0.8 opt (E).
drivers.maint_capex_pct_op__source: Van replacement ~$30-38k per van every ~6-7 years (E) = ~$5k/van/yr; 3 vans ~$15k vs base y5 op ~$100-150k => ~10%; tools/ladders/racks extra.
drivers.reserve_months__source: Seasonal swings (cold-snap spring failures vs slow late-summer installs, E) and van/insurance shocks; 2 months of cash costs, 3 in conservative.
drivers.founder_draw_per_month__source: Stage E standardization: $4k/mo from month 13 in all scenarios.
drivers.tax_rate_pct__source: Stage E standardization: 30% blended pass-through estimate.

staff.notes: First technician hired when prior-month jobs reach ~60 (founder's own capacity ~3 jobs/day while also selling and dispatching), then one per +60 jobs/month (~3 jobs/day). Loaded pay: Chicago median $65,090 x1.25 [C, DF-S006] = $6.8k/mo + van insurance/maintenance ~$1.1k/mo (E). Capex/hire = used van, racks, tools, opening parts (E). Stage D threshold was 50 (Correction: hired into the conservative plateau of ~62 jobs and produced an artifact loss).
Chicago dispatcher median $58,900; CSR median $47,100 [C, DF-S033]; loaded x1.2 (E).
E — frees founder from field supervision.

overhead.notes: Commercial auto avg $245/mo small-business policy [D, DF-S034] + maintenance (E).

overhead.notes: Home Repair Act minimums $100k/$300k BI, $50k PD, $10k improper repair [A, WS18-S010]; GL small-biz avg $45/mo is a floor [D, DF-S034]; contractor rating higher (E).
Housecall Pro Essentials $149-189/mo [B, DF-S035] + AI receptionist/answering (~$150-200/mo, E).
E; Chicago Home Repair licence $1,000 per 2-year term [A, E-WS18035-S004] only if working in Chicago; suburban registrations MISSING.

overhead.notes: E — small flex unit in NW Cook/DuPage.
